description: Golden parser fixtures (T04-03/T04-04, ADR-0002): multi-language source -> expected units {unit_kind, byte span, local_name, kind, anchor, parent} and classified unresolved references. Each case declares its `language` (TypeScript in T04-03, JavaScript in T04-04, Rust in T04-05, Python in T24-01 per ADR-0015). Implementation-specific sig hashes / full serialized locators are pinned in crate-local goldens, not here (neutrality for cross-language reuse).

cases.title: Core declaration kinds each become a symbol unit

provenance.source: T04-03 (authored); TypeScript adapter over tree-sitter tsx

cases.title: Method and nested function parents
Overload signatures share a route but differ by signature
Anonymous / computed names fall back to ordinal anchors
Module specifiers become classified unresolved references
An empty file is a single empty file unit
A whitespace-only file is a single file unit
Malformed input recovers symbols and yields a fallback chunk
Byte spans are byte offsets across multi-byte characters
Core JavaScript declaration kinds each become a symbol unit
JavaScript method and nested function parents
Computed method names fall back to ordinal anchors
JavaScript module specifiers become classified unresolved references
An empty JavaScript file is a single empty file unit
A whitespace-only JavaScript file is a single file unit
Malformed JavaScript recovers symbols and yields a fallback chunk
JavaScript byte spans are byte offsets across multi-byte characters
Core Rust item kinds each become a symbol unit
impl methods are parented and routed through the Self type
Items nested in a module are parented to the module
use paths become classified unresolved references
An empty Rust file is a single empty file unit
A whitespace-only Rust file is a single file unit
Malformed Rust recovers symbols and yields a fallback chunk
Rust byte spans are byte offsets across multi-byte characters
Core Python declaration kinds each become a symbol unit
cases.source:
def foo(a):
    return a
async def bar():
    pass
class Baz:
    pass
X = 1
Y: int = 2

cases.title: Methods are parented to their class and nested defs to their enclosing def
A decorated definition is one unit that owns the decorators' span

provenance.note: T24-01 decision: the unit is the decorated_definition wrapper (span starts at the first `@`), its kind and route are the definition's, and the inner definition is not a second unit.

cases.title: Import specifiers become one classified unresolved reference each
cases.source:
import os, sys
import numpy as np
from pkg.mod import a, b
from . import sibling

cases.title: An empty Python file is a single empty file unit
A whitespace-only Python file is a single file unit
Malformed Python recovers symbols and yields a fallback chunk
Python byte spans are byte offsets across multi-byte characters
Both function forms and the declaration commands each become a symbol unit
A declaration inside a function body nests under it (captured at any depth)
Only source/. produce references, and only from their first argument
cases.source:
source lib.sh
. ./other.sh
echo hi
ls -la
source extra.sh arg1

cases.title: One unit per declaration command; an operand-less or plain assignment is none
Two indistinguishable declarations of one name demote to ordinal anchors
An empty Bash file is a single empty file unit
A whitespace-only Bash file is a single file unit
Malformed Bash yields a fallback chunk and still names the definition inside it
Bash byte spans are byte offsets across multi-byte characters
Each Go declaration kind becomes a named symbol unit
A grouped type/const/var block yields one named unit per spec
A spec declaring several names is one unit named by the first
cases.source:
package main

const C, D = 3, 4

var a, b int

cases.title: A type or var declared in a function body routes under it
Every import spec is one reference to its path, never to its alias
Identically named methods on different receivers both keep the named route
An empty Go file is a single empty file unit
A whitespace-only Go file is a single file unit
Malformed Go yields a fallback chunk and the following declaration is still named
Go byte spans are byte offsets across multi-byte characters
A Cargo.toml excerpt is sectioned by its table headers, not by its first keys
cases.source:
[package]
name = "demo"
version = "0.1.0"

[dependencies]
serde = "1"
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }

[[bin]]
name = "a"

cases.title: A key before the first table header is a top-level section
A sub-table is a sibling named by its dotted key, not a nested section
Bare, quoted and dotted keys all name their section
A key with a space is no path segment: the section takes an ordinal anchor
Two [[bin]] elements are indistinguishable by signature and take ordinals
An empty TOML file is a single empty file unit
A whitespace-only TOML file is a single file unit
Malformed TOML yields a fallback chunk and the following table is still named
A non-ASCII TOML key must be quoted, and spans stay byte offsets
A three-document manifest yields three documents, not one flat key list
cases.source:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
spec:
  ports:
    - 80
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
---
kind: Ingress

cases.title: A key is a section only when its value is a mapping or a sequence
cases.source:
apiVersion: v1
metadata:
  name: app
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app

cases.title: A document whose single key spans it all is still the key's ancestor (D-135)
cases.source:
metadata:
  name: app
  labels:
    app: demo

cases.title: A key containing `/` takes an ordinal anchor rather than corrupting the route
An empty YAML file is a single empty file unit
A whitespace-only YAML file has no document at all
Malformed YAML yields a fallback chunk and the following key is still named
A YAML key needs no quoting to be non-ASCII, and spans stay byte offsets
